seam_rule_off_reproduces_ib_pr_452.what_ran: date_basis_grading.account_day over every account-day of the 85 graded days, the repeated-share rule OFF (second_witness_grades_security_day(..., repeated_share_rule=False) for each security-day), the nine admitted pairs read from the transactions table by date_basis_grading.second_witness_admits, serving by date_basis_grading.serving_rule

window_proposed.population: the 300 securities of the nine admitted pairs outside the first witness with a reader bar (of 305 with a ticker); every count is over those securities and the 85 graded days
window_proposed.reason: 40 trading days (about two calendar months), the day graded included. Over the 300 securities of the nine pairs outside the first witness with bars and the 85 graded days, the rule takes, by window (securities taken on one or more days / security-days un-graded beyond the guard / securities graded on some days and taken on others / account-days no longer freed): 10: 30 / 233 / 27 / 156; 20: 22 / 255 / 18 / 241; 40: 14 / 272 / 8 / 287; 60: 14 / 325 / 7 / 341; 85: 14 / 372 / 7 / 374. A short window lets a spell of a few repeated bars take a security that otherwise moves: 27 and 18 securities change verdict inside the run at 10 and 20 days. From 40 days the set of securities taken stops growing (14 at 40, 14 at 60, 14 at 85) and the number that change verdict settles (8 at 40; 7 at 60; 7 at 85), while a longer window costs more freed account-days (287 at 40, 341 at 60, 374 at 85) and un-grades more security-days for want of history (54, 93, 134). 40 is the shortest window at which the verdicts have settled. THE TRADE, plainly: a fixed window is reproducible (the same security-day, the same grade, whatever the run) but it is not the whole-run reading v0.43 wrote. The seven securities of IB-pr-452 not graded on any day cost 33 account-days and 1 account; the 40-day window takes those seven and 7 more, each on part of the run, and costs 287 account-days and 2 accounts. The row-days un-graded by the rule on the days it does not grade are most on EIBIX, VMLUX, OLCYX (3328, 342, 147 row-days): securities near the one-half edge are un-graded on the days a window finds more than half repeated and graded on the others.
window_proposed.when_fewer_bars_than_the_window: A security-day with fewer than 20 days compared in its window (half the window, rounded up: min_days_compared) gets NO grade from the second witness with the rule on: a share taken from fewer days is not a measurement, and a comparison the instrument cannot make is not a pass (v0.41's spirit). At or above 20 compared days the share is taken over the days that exist. With the rule off (the guard alone) the floor does not apply. The window is the 40 trading days of the calendar ending at the graded day and reads no bar outside it; a day is compared only when both it and its prior trading day are inside the window, so at most 39 days are compared. At the first graded day 2026-06-10, 296 of 300 securities have the full 39 comparisons and 4 are below the floor.
window_proposed.window_definition: the REPEATED_SHARE_WINDOW trading days of lib/trading_calendar ending at the graded day, the graded day included; nothing before the window is read
window_proposed.candidates_note: securities_taken = securities (CUSIPs) on which the guard grades a security-day and the rule does not, on one or more of the 85 graded days; securities_whose_verdict_changes_within_the_run = of those, the ones the rule also graded (with the guard) on one or more days; the 85-day candidate is the whole run as the window, graded per day

securities_by_share_of_repeated_days.over_what: the securities of the nine admitted pairs that sit OUTSIDE the first witness (behind an OUTSIDE_ANCHOR row of the sizing's account-days, cash rule in force) and have at least one usable reader bar: 300 securities (of 305 of those nine pairs with a ticker); share of repeated days at the LAST graded day (2026-10-09), over the 40 trading days ending there (the proposed window): repeated_days / days_compared, a day compared when the security has a bar on it and on its prior trading day, both inside the window; 0 securities have no day compared and are not counted
securities_by_share_of_repeated_days.bin_rule_in_words: ten bins of width one tenth; a share exactly on an edge goes to the UPPER bin (0.5 is in 0.5-0.6; 0.1 is in 0.1-0.2); a share of exactly 1.0 (every compared day repeated) goes to the last bin, 0.9-1.0. More than half repeated = the shares in 0.5-0.6 and above, except exactly 0.5.
securities_by_share_of_repeated_days.overlap_over_what: the securities BOTH witnesses carry (held on one or more of the 85 graded days, carried by the anchor with a positive close on one or more of them, with a ticker that is not the CUSIP: 894, IB-pr-439 counted 894) whose type is one of the nine admitted pairs (698) and that have a reader bar (694); the same share, day and window; 1 have no day compared

securities_taken_by_the_rule_cost.basis: securities taken = taken on ONE OR MORE of the 85 graded days at the proposed window (the guard grades the security-day, the repeated-share rule does not); cost = the rule-off nine-pair sizing less the sizing under the rule; row_days = rows of those securities in the sizing's account-days (an account's row on a day)

the_seven_whole_run_cost.basis: the nine-pair sizing with the repeated-share rule OFF (the guard alone), and these seven tickers given no grade on any of the 85 days: freed and never-served against the rule-off sizing

fetch.reader: fetch_yahoo (data/assets/scripts/silver/commonwealth_price_basis_census.py) / read_yahoo_close (data/assets/scripts/silver/commonwealth_daily_valuation.py), neither edited; unadjusted Close

not_established: That 40 trading days is the right window: several were measured and one is proposed; the CTO writes the contract.  The short-history floor (half the window) is chosen, not derived.
Why a security's bar repeats (a stale feed, a fund that does not move, a late publication): the counts cannot tell them apart, and the rule does not try.

That the securities the rule takes beyond IB-pr-452's seven are wrongly graded by the second witness: they repeat on about half their days and are taken on part of the run; nothing here says their moved bars are dated wrong.
That a freed account-day's claim would be correct: freed account-days are a count of account-days no witness is barred from grading, not a check that the claim is right.
The distribution on any day but the last graded day (2026-10-09).
The overlap securities' sizing: they are counted in tenths only; the first witness grades them and the rule would not touch a claim of the first witness.
Anything outside the 85 graded days, the 878 tickers asked, or the securities with no ticker, no type, mixed types or another type (not graded, not counted in the tenths).
The 7 tickers for which the reader returned nothing: their rows block their account-days (the module gives no grade without a bar).
Whether the sizing under the rule would be the sizing a producer reads: no producer, schema or schedule exists; nothing is served and no claim is re-graded in the product.
